title: The Hilton entertainment director and the four-wall idea
summary: A liberal Hilton director invited Monk in and suggested four-walling, but died of a heart attack.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: I was here, and into it again. Really into it. By this time, now, I'm carrying around a little briefcase, trying to talk to this guy, trying to talk to that entertainment director. Can't see this one, trying to talk to somebody that knew that one...
So you were assaulting the hotels?

Right. I spoke to one guy, and I felt like I had really made a breakthrough. It was at the Hilton. And he had the reputation of being one of the most liberal-minded of them all. It was Dave...David...oh, God, I forgot that man's name... I think I'll mention it in a minute. And he was the entertainment director for the Hilton. And he had been over to the Caesar's for a lot of years, and at one time he had brought in Jimmy Smith. He tried it with...he had Duke Ellington and he had, he brought in Sarah Vaughan. He said he tried it at Caesar's and it never really worked out for him when he brought some of the jazz people up.

And I called him to make an appointment with him, and he said, 'Well, come on in.' And that shocked me, because he was ready, here, he invited me in. I didn't think it would happen at a major hotel, that major hotel, the Hilton. But it was because of the man, you see, the entertainment director.

And I met with him that day and when I...By that time, when I got to him -- and he was a nice man -- and we started talking. I exploded. I was unloading, because I had somebody listening, and I didn't have good tactics. He said, 'Wait, wait a minute, Monk. Don't...Wait, don't get excited.'

Yeah. He said, 'Don't get excited. You don't have to sell me.' He said, 'I see it in your face. I know about your track record. I'm in agreement with you, but that's not the way it's done. It's not the way it's done.' He said, 'Now, what I'd suggest is this. I will give you an attempt, and try and work with you. I can't go to the hotel and convince them that you have this room to bring jazz into, and so-and-so, but I've got a young man that I work with on certain things. We'll have you to four-wall the place, I want you to four-wall it. You can bring in what you want to bring.'

But what did I know? All I knew was like I was a bull in a china closet. Garrett Asif (?), who is a big promoter now in rock and all that sort of thing, that was the one I was going to talk to, to get it on. So I went and met with Garrett Asif. Garry wasn't into jazz but he was into promoting, and making money. And lo and behold, the old man died, heart attack. He

passed away.

That was my first hope and it looked like everything went down with him because he was a nice man, to receive me the way he did. And he understood what I was trying to say. He had a capacity for the music.
